page.layout: Two columns of running text on one printed page, both set as full justified lines with no marginal notes. Page number and running head at the top. Heading "De grandioribus alitibus." stands on its own line above the second paragraph of text, with a large woodcut-style initial "A" opening that paragraph. No notes in either margin.

main_text.p: victos passim occultatos neminem latere putárunt, quafi aveillic minime mansura, fi hominum quisquam adesset. Itaque factum est, vt filentio noctis fecutæ Imperator ad suos euaserit, & falutis suæ caulam expo-suerit.

A quo tempore Tartari bubonem seu auem felicem, aufpicatam & sacram reue-rentur, plumasque ejus ceu amuletum & profperitatis causam in capitibus gestant, ac felices se prædicant, quicunque eas habe-re possunt.
main_text.head: De grandioribus alitibus.
main_text.p: Vium grandissimi & pene bestiarum generis sunt Struthocameli. In Africa & Æthiopia altitudinem equitis infi-dentis equo excedunt, celeritate vincunt, nec tamen volucres, nec a terra tolluntur. Xenophon expeditionis Cyri lib. 1. tradit in Arabia repertos Struthocamelos, quos nemo ex toto exercitu capere potuerit. Athenæus Arabicos Regum Persarum mensis epulis, adhibest foli-tos scripsit. Galenus quoque in ciborum cen-tu eos reposuit, horum alas deteriores caterasque superiores lucrum alius non esse promisit, carnes tamen ex-crementis abunde refertas concoctione, esse pertinaces. Concoquendi fine delectu devorant.

page.notes: Printed page with running text in two columns, the second column beginning with the heading. Several words are uncertain in the scan: the Latin is set in a heavy, faded type and some lines are partly obscured by show-through from the reverse, so the reading above is a best attempt at the text and should be checked against the scan. Words I could not read with confidence are marked where they stand. The page is heavily damaged along its right edge and bottom, and the final line on the lower right is partly illegible.
